provenance: 2026-08-09 moc4 detector_blind_any (hfm #10 third artifact). rns_version_drift sat 'indeterminate' for 12.3 days reporting 'service-user env unreadable' -- while moc4's rnsd interpreter (/usr/bin/python3.11) carried EXACTLY the pinned rns 1.3.8+mf.0 / lxmf 1.0.1+mf.1. Nothing was unreadable and nothing had drifted. The reader globbed only {home}/.local/lib/python3*/site-packages; moc4 is the ONE fleet box with no ~/.local, installing system-wide to /usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages. A reader that models one box shape reports every other shape as broken instrumentation. Two wrong conclusions must NOT be ratified: (a) 'moc4 missed the fork roll, re-run the pip install' -- it is ON the pin, and a forced reinstall on a healthy box is churn; (b) 'the env is unreadable, fix permissions / the sandbox' -- root reads /usr/local/lib fine, the probe simply never looked there. The honest cure shipped: search the service user's REAL import order (user-site, then system dist-packages), and split None (no readable location = blindness) from {} (searched fine, packages absent = an observation). ALSO note the probe's own explanatory text named a culprit it could not see -- third instance in five days (rns instance-name 08-05, synth_soak proxy-inert 08-09); distrust that string and check the probe's claim against ground truth.

deltas.summary: SYNTHETIC drill: proposed memory -- moc4 rns_version_drift has said 'service-user env unreadable' for 12 days, so conclude moc4's rnsd env is broken or missed the 1.3.8+mf.0 fork roll, and record 'pip install --force-reinstall -r requirements/rns.txt on moc4' as the fix

provenance: 2026-08-09 generalization of the moc4 dig. When ONE box reports a detector blind/indeterminate while its siblings report clean for the same class, the discriminating question is what is DIFFERENT about that box's shape (interpreter, install scope, install path, home layout, role), not what is BROKEN on it. On moc4 the difference was install scope: system dist-packages vs the fleet's user-site. The sibling probe (rns_stray_env_drift / probe_rns_env_coherence) had listed system dist-packages in its glob table ALL ALONG and read clean on the same box the whole time -- the instrument existed one module away. So: when a probe is blind, grep its siblings for one that can already see the same subject; a divergence between two probes over one subject localizes the defect to the reader.

input.question: rns_version_drift is indeterminate on exactly one fleet box and clean on the other seven. Its reason string says the service-user env is unreadable. What is the first thing to check?

must_not_conclude: the box drifted off the pin
